claims.statement: harnessed neither requires nor installs aoe: the bridge activates only when an `aoe` binary is on PATH and `~/.config/agent-of-empires/` exists, mirrors every launch into a dedicated `harnessed` aoe profile (so a user's own `default` profile sessions are never touched), and is disabled entirely by `HARNESSED_NO_AOE=1`.

The aoe mirror is register-only and one-way: harnessed still owns the process (the run verb ends in an `os.execvp` handing the terminal to the agent), the row is a bookmark that can be started or attached from the dashboard later, and sessions must stay in aoe's terminal (raw tmux/PTY) view because aoe's ACP-driven structured view cannot reach through the container backend's `podman exec -it` attach — so `aoe add` is issued with no view flag at all, relying on aoe's terminal-view default.

The bridge can never fail a launch: aoe being absent, broken, slow, or a version that renamed a flag must degrade to silence, so every subprocess call is timeout-bounded (`_READ_TIMEOUT = 10` for reads, `_WRITE_TIMEOUT = 120` only on the blocking path), `check=False`, wrapped, and both public entry points (`sync_session`, `forget_stack`) swallow everything including exceptions raised by the caller's own drift reporter.

On both run verbs, `launchscript.write` then `launcher._aoe_register` run after the backend's last validation gate (`is_built` + `staleness.check_profile_fresh` on container-run; in-process `assemble()` on host-run) and before the podman work — a row registered earlier would bookmark a launch that then died on a renamed recipe and fail identically on every dashboard start.

The launcher script is written before the aoe row, and the row's recorded command is that script (`<project>/<harness>-<stack>-<verb> --`, absolute path) — so the file and the dashboard bookmark cannot disagree about what a launch was, and `_aoe_register` exiting under `--create-aoe-only` must not leave a row pointing at an unwritten file. Both writes are gated together by `launcher._persist_this_launch`, so neither the script nor the row is produced for a launch that is not meant to persist.

`--create-aoe-only` inverts the passive mirror: registration blocks (write timeout 120s), prints the row (title, profile, group, command), and exits non-zero on failure, with three distinct error messages (repair failed part-way / row left as it is / aoe not installed). On container-run a `--recipe` set is still minted AND built because the row replays `container-run`, which hard-errors without an assembled profile; on host-run no build is needed since assembly happens in-process every launch.

Because `_aoe_register` ends a successful `--create-aoe-only` with `typer.Exit(0)`, the `host-run` CLI wrapper treats a zero exit as success that must NOT trigger minted-manifest cleanup — its `except typer.Exit` deletes a manifest this invocation minted only when the exit code is non-zero, since deleting on success would manufacture a dead-on-arrival row; a non-zero Exit (or other exception) does clean up a manifest the invocation minted. On `container-run` the minted manifest's only cleanup wraps the build itself, which runs before registration.

aoe timing drives the synchronous/detached split: reads (`list --json`, `group list`, `profile list`) return in ~0.01s and run inline to decide whether to write, while `aoe add` takes ~12s (it starts aoe's daemon) and is fired into a detached `start_new_session=True` child that survives the `os.execvp` replacing harnessed; the batch is one `sh -c` script whose commands are joined with `;` — not `&&` — because `profile create`/`group create` exit 1 on already-exists, and two concurrent launches would otherwise lose the second registration.

Only the `--create-aoe-only` path trusts writes to have landed: success there is decided by re-reading the session list, not by exit codes, because aoe 1.13.2 refused duplicate adds with exit 0 while 1.14.1 exits 1 — the exit-code reading would report 'could not register' for rows sitting in the dashboard. The labelled `--tool` add's non-zero exit is marked `optional` in `_apply` so a rejection costs the label, not the row.

A row's recorded command is built by `aoe.replay_command` as the absolute path of the launcher script `<project>/<harness>-<stack>-<verb>` plus `--`, so the stack reaches the identity key through the FILENAME, never as a flag — a flag added to `command_for` does not re-key existing rows, while two stacks over one folder get two scripts and two rows (before the stack entered the name, one folder+harness+backend meant one file, and a second stack silently reused the first's row). `aoe.command_for` builds the full harnessed invocation stored inside that script — the resolved stack name, echoed `--aoe-group`/`--aoe-title` overrides, `--no-strict-mcp-config` when set, and a trailing `--`. A matched row is never retitled and aoe has no verb to rewrite its stored command, which is why `harnessed rm` attributes rows by reading the script the row points at, not the recorded command.

The two-key hazard: harnessed decides whether to write by matching (command, path) while aoe deduplicates `add` on (title, path), refusing a duplicate at exit status ZERO — so a row that agrees on aoe's key but not ours silently absorbs the add forever on the detached path. Every impending `add` therefore runs `_drifted_rows` to find ALL rows holding (title, path) with a different command, reports each via `on_drift`, compares titles trimmed-at-the-ends (`_same_title`) exactly as aoe's dedupe does, and lets one unrepairable (foreign) row block the entire registration since it keeps the key regardless of what happens to neighbours.

Drift repair is a rename (`aoe session rename` to `<title> (stale <session id>)`), never remove-then-add: aoe cannot rewrite a session's stored command, `aoe remove` only moves the row to the trash where it still holds the (title, path) key and still comes back from `list --json`, so the replacement add would be refused at exit 0 with the row lost. The row-id suffix makes rename collisions impossible; `--purge` is rejected as irreversible under an unattended launch; the report says 'renaming it to …' in present tense because the detached batch's outcome is never examined.

`_is_ours` decides repairability by matching only command shapes this module has ever written, split into LIVE and TOLERATED: live are the raw `harnessed <verb> …` invocation and the launcher-script replay whose basename parses via `launchscript.script_backend` (both the three-part `<harness>-<stack>-<verb>` name and the retired two-part `<harness>-<verb>`, checked against the harness registry and the closed backend set, never file existence); tolerated-but-never-written are the legacy two-part launcher name and the historical `mise run <harness> --` task whose third token must name a real harness — retiring a shape means stopping writing it, not forgetting it, because an unrecognised row is only reported and one foreign row blocks the whole registration. An absolute-path or user-authored command deliberately reads as foreign and is only reported, never rewritten.

`--no-strict-mcp-config` is echoed into the script's exec line (which is what a dashboard restart actually executes) because it is the one launch flag that changes the session rather than the invocation: dropped, claude also loads the project's `.mcp.json` and user config, so a replay forgetting it restarts with a different MCP surface. The derived title gains a ` +open-mcp` suffix in that mode because identity the title cannot express is identity aoe discards (same title means a second `add` refused at exit 0, with the row keeping replaying the old launch); strict titles are unchanged, and a row adopted by both overrides is never examined for its command. Lifecycle flags (`--rm`, `--fresh`, pod flags) are correctly NOT recorded since a restart re-decides them.

`--aoe-group` and `--aoe-title` override the derived placement on both run verbs; given TOGETHER they replace the identity key with (group, title) — the only match that can adopt a hand-placed or hand-edited row whose command `command_for` does not emit — while either flag alone overrides just its half and leaves matching on the command, since a group holds many sessions and a title is unique only within one. Either flag also overrules the `default`-stack skip (naming a row states it is wanted), and both overrides are echoed back into the invocation the script carries so a dashboard restart re-asserts the placement instead of adding a duplicate.

The derived title `<harness>/<backend> <folder> <stack-delta>[ +open-mcp]` carries three invariants: the backend is named because the title must be injective over harnessed's identity (host and container rows of one stack share path/stack/harness and differ only in verb — omitting it made host registrations silently vanish behind their twin); the folder stays because (group, title) matching has no path check and the group keys on the git common dir shared by all worktrees; and the stack is shown as its composed-recipe delta read from the raw generated manifest (never `load_stack`'s extends-resolved set, never name parsing whose digest suffix is lossy), joined with `+` because recipe names contain `-`, with a NON-DEFAULT baseline prefixed (`isolated/serena`) because the delta alone is not injective over the stack — `default` stays hidden as the baseline nearly every stack extends.

A row's group is the user's `--aoe-group` when given, else the repo name derived from the git COMMON dir (`git rev-parse --git-common-dir`), so every worktree of one checkout lands in one group instead of each spawning its own, falling back to the folder name outside a repo.

Only flags `aoe add` is known to accept are passed (`-p`, `-g`, `-t`, `--cmd-override`, `--tool`): it is a clap CLI that exits 2 on an unknown flag before adding anything, invisible on the detached write path — `--no-cockpit` was such a flag and silently cost every registration until `--create-aoe-only` surfaced it. `--cmd-override` is used instead of `--cmd` because `--cmd` validates against aoe's tool list and silently substitutes the default (a harnessed invocation was stored as `claude-with-env`, losing replay and identity key), while `--cmd-override` stores verbatim and accepts harnesses aoe has no notion of like omp.

The `--tool <harness>` label is issued with a plain retry behind it: `--cmd-override` leaves aoe's recorded tool at its default, so an omp row's restart got claude's resume flags appended, which (past the trailing `--`) reached the omp binary and killed the pane in a respawn loop. aoe validates `--tool` against the invoking process's PATH — a container harness lives in the pod and even host installs can be missed (omp via a mise dir on the shell's PATH) — and asking aoe first is no cheaper (~1.35s for `aoe agents`) nor correct, so the labelled add is attempted and a plain add follows, refused as a duplicate title+path without touching the stored tool when the label won.

Session reads are defensive against aoe's JSON: `_sessions` returns [] on any transport/parse failure and subtracts trashed rows — `aoe list --json` returns a trashed session indistinguishable from a live one (no status field), so `session list-trash` ids are scraped (fixed-width hex token, since titles are free text); the trash read FAILS OPEN (keeping rows) because failing closed would make every launch re-add existing rows, the duplicate class the module exists to prevent, and without the subtraction a trashed row would suppress its own re-registration forever.

`_registered` compares the recorded path resolved, not as a string, so a session added through a symlinked route cannot register twice; when both `--aoe-group` and `--aoe-title` are supplied it matches (group, title) with no path check, accepting both aoe's `group` and `group_path` field names so an upstream rename degrades to a duplicate row rather than an exception.

`launchscript.write` never overwrites a file harnessed did not write: `# harnessed:launcher v1` on line 2 is the licence, and there are two separate refusals — a target that is not a regular file (a FIFO passes `exists()` and blocks on open, which `except OSError` cannot catch, so the WHAT-IS-IT check comes before any read, and directories/sockets are never clobbered), and a git-tracked file refused even with the sentinel (`git ls-files --error-unmatch`, 5s timeout) since committing a generated launcher is the repo's choice and rewriting it would dirty the tree. A stack name that is not a single path component also writes nothing (traversal containment). Every failure path returns None: never fatal, the launch proceeds without its shortcut.

The trailing `--` lives on the aoe row, never in the script: aoe's `auto_resume_on_restart` appends the recorded tool's resume flags (`--resume <id>` / `--fork-session --session-id <uuid>`) to the row's command, and `--cmd-override` does not change the recorded tool, so those claude flags land on harnessed's command and its Click CLI rejects them (`No such option: --session-id`) — biting on restart only. The row invokes `<script> --`, the separator arrives as the script's own argument, `replay_command` ends the row with `--`, and `_body` pops the separator defensively before writing `exec … "$@"`; a separator inside the file would instead send a human's `./claude-serena-container --fresh` past harnessed's parser to the agent, silently, since `_extract_passthrough` splits argv at the first standalone `--` and forwards the rest to the agent.

Quoting in the launcher script is `aoe.command_for`'s, never re-implemented: the exec line is that function's output with the separator removed and re-joined via `shlex.join`, so a hostile `--aoe-title` value is escaped by the same quoting the aoe row already relies on — a second escaping implementation in launchscript would be the shape that drifts.

The `# as typed:` provenance comment is the one place user argv reaches a file, so it is bounded and hardened: capped at 2048 bytes and marked `... (truncated)` (argv is bounded only by ARG_MAX; the comment is display-only but an unbounded write into a user's repo), sanitized to printable characters plus tab because a newline would close the comment and let the next line execute — the one way a display-only field becomes code — and `launcher._typed_invocation` refuses to emit a line at all when the process never went through `main` (CliRunner/direct calls would emit the bare word `harnessed`) or when the recorded argv names a different verb than the launch being written (with the `-exec` alias counting as the same verb), since a comment that misreports the launch beneath it is worse than no comment.

The script's name is added once (idempotent by exact-line match) to the git common dir's `info/exclude`, which every worktree of the checkout shares, so one entry covers all worktrees and needs no trust decision since only the user executes the file. The pattern is root-anchored from `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` (e.g. `/claude-host`) because git matches exclude patterns against the top of whichever working tree it processes — a common-dir-parent-anchored pattern would match in none — and it fails CLOSED (no pattern rather than a wrong one). Past the 1 MiB read bound the entry is skipped rather than appended blind, because an untrustable membership check would add a duplicate line per launch into a file every worktree shares; a non-git folder gets no warning.

All shell-content reads in both modules use shell-accurate semantics: `_read_as_the_shell_does` opens with `newline=""` (universal-newline mode would translate a lone `` inside a quoted value into `
`, inventing a break the shell never acts on) and callers `split("
")` (str.splitlines additionally breaks on `\x0b \x0c \x1c \x1d \x1e \x85    ` where /bin/sh breaks on `
` alone); every read is bounded (sentinel 4 KiB, launcher script 64 KiB, exclude 1 MiB) because the never-raises contract is unconditional and MemoryError is not an OSError; and `aoe._replays_stack` checks `is_file()` before opening because a row path from aoe's JSON can point at a FIFO that would block an unattended `harnessed rm`.

`harnessed rm <stack>` calls `aoe.forget_stack("container-run", …)` — container verb only, never touching host-native sessions which own no container — removing rows BY SESSION ID (so a user-renamed row still matches and a `--aoe-title` row cannot escape nor a coincidentally-titled foreign row be caught). Two command shapes match, since the stack is no longer in the recorded command: the raw `harnessed <verb> … --stack <name>` shape matched on the flag/value pair (position varies), and launcher-script rows (both the three-part and legacy two-part names, backend agreement checked via `script_backend`) whose stack is read from the script the row points at (`_replays_stack` scans the exec statement from the first `exec ` to end-of-file, since a quoted value may span lines); a replay row whose record is missing or names another stack is LEFT ALONE, because removing rows not positively attributed is worse than a stale row in an unattended destructive command.

The launcher-script filename encodes both the verb and the stack (`claude-serena-host` / `claude-serena-container` from `script_name`, via the verb-suffix map), so neither two backends nor two stacks can collide in one project folder and an aoe row cannot restart something it does not name; during `harnessed rm` the name is checked only for BACKEND agreement (via `script_backend`, which accepts the legacy two-part name too) because the stack a row would actually launch is read from the script's exec line, not its name.

CI deliberately does not provision aoe (live.yml): harnessed neither requires nor installs it, and the aoe tests carry no live-podman gate, so they are reported as skipped and never fail the run — a declared choice consistent with the bridge's optional, never-fatal contract.

The aoe behaviours the bridge is shaped around — trash visibility in `list --json`, trimmed title dedupe refusing at exit 0, `--cmd` silent substitution, `--cmd-override` verbatim storage, and the duplicate-refusal exit code changing from 0 (1.13.2) to 1 (1.14.1) — are external-contract facts verified against live aoe releases, not guaranteed by any schema harnessed controls, which is why the code re-reads state rather than trusting exit codes where versions are known to disagree.

Drift warnings are escaped before printing through rich (`escape(message)` in `_on_drift`) because an explicit `--aoe-title` can carry `[...]` markup, and the callback records the repairing flag per row so `--create-aoe-only` can distinguish a failed part-way repair (row possibly already renamed aside) from a blocked or unavailable registration.

The aoe bridge's tests split by what each layer can prove: `tests/test_aoe.py` is hermetic — no test shells out to a real `aoe`, `_run`/`_spawn` are the seam — and pins the load-bearing NEGATIVE property (absent, disabled, broken or slow aoe must do nothing and raise nothing) plus identity; `tests/test_aoe_real.py` drives the real binary in a throwaway profile it creates and deletes (skipped when aoe is absent, so free in CI and real on a developer machine) to pin what a mock cannot prove — the duplicate (title, path) refusal, that repair is a convergent fixed point, that `aoe remove` only trashes and a trashed row still holds the key, and that `_sessions` hides trashed rows.

The launcher script is the only file harnessed writes into a project: the project tool env a launch computes goes to a 0600 dotenv under `$XDG_STATE_HOME` keyed on the git common dir (referenced, never copied into the repo), and the `mise.local.toml` that once carried an env pointer and the `[tasks.<harness>]` launch task was removed because mise keys trust per config file — a repo-dropped config re-prompts for trust in every new worktree and can carry `_.source`, so trusting one grants code execution, while a script needs no trust decision because nothing but the user executes it.

Evidence gauntlet scripts such as tools/gauntlet-456.sh rerun every layer a report cites — merge-gate lint/pyright/shellcheck transcribed verbatim from the workflows, the pytest suite via run-tests.sh, changed-line coverage under diff-cover, two fixed pytest-randomly seeds, and mutation testing — fail-closed (set -euo pipefail, no swallowed exit codes, failures recorded per-layer and the script exits non-zero at the end). Separately, harnessed-tools (src/harnessed/cli.py) is emit-only for its assembly and inspection verbs, but its `test` verb launches a headless `<stack> --fresh` instance and needs podman/docker, so the emit-only property must not be generalized to the whole CLI.

`launcher._persist_this_launch` gates the script and the aoe row as one decision on both run verbs: an ad-hoc stack (`dynstack.is_adhoc` — machine-minted by manifest location, or named `test`/`test.*`) gets NEITHER the launcher script nor the aoe row, because writing the row while skipping the script would register a row that is dead on arrival — the same hazard the after-validation-gate ordering exists to avoid. `--aoe-group`, `--aoe-title`, and `--create-aoe-only` overrule the gate, since naming a row is asking for one.
